name: Poland

observations.reasoning: Sourced on 2026-07-27, transversal pass over the population indicator. Population on 1 January 2025: 36497495 inhabitants, recorded as 36.497 million. Eurostat dataset demo_pjan, Population on 1 January by age and sex, read through the dissemination API on 2026-07-27, dataset last updated 2026-07-09. Total population, both sexes, all ages, which is exactly what this indicator's denominator asks for. Read as one table covering every country in the record, so no value here is derived from a neighbour: each is that country's own row. The previous value was an opening estimate produced with no source and no research.

Read on 2026-07-27 from the Local Data Bank of GUS, subject P2874, variable 194944, 'widowiska w stałych salach teatralnych - przedstawienia: teatr lalkowy', national level: 7 812 performances in 2024, seen by 935 249 spectators. The series holds far steadier than the institution count — 8 820 in 2019, 7 863 in 2022, 7 973 in 2023 — so Poland lost seven puppet institutions over five years and about a ninth of its performances. Disputed on scope, and the scope is in the variable's own name. 'W stałych salach teatralnych' means in permanent theatre halls: this counts what the puppet theatres played at home and drops everything they played on tour. For a sector whose companies spend much of the year in school halls that is not a rounding error, and the true figure is above 7 812 by an unknown margin. The broader GUS measures that do count by place of presentation, in subject P1680, carry no breakdown by kind of theatre, so the choice was between the right genre with the wrong scope and the right scope with no genre. The first is recorded, with its scope named. Basis 'organisation': GUS classes the institution, not the production.

Read on 2026-07-27 from the Local Data Bank of GUS, subject P2874 'Teatry', variable 194943, 'jednostki: teatr lalkowy', national level: 28 puppet theatre institutions in 2024. The series falls steadily — 35 in 2019, 29 in 2022 and 2023, 28 in 2024 — so Poland has lost a fifth of its puppet institutions in five years, which is the most useful thing this figure says. Disputed on one filter, not on the reading. GUS counts the institutions that file the theatre return and classes them by kind of theatre; it does not sort them by who backs them. The denominator here asks for public backing, and 28 is therefore a ceiling: every publicly backed puppet house is inside it, and any private one that files a return is inside it too. What would settle it is the register of instytucje kultury held by the ministry and the local authorities, read against this list of 28. The reading is exact; the question is whether the denominators match. The opening estimate was 22 to 28 and its upper bound turns out to be the sourced ceiling, which is luck rather than method.

Web check of 2026-07-27, searched in the country's own language. Two establishments retained, both read at source. First, the Puppetry Faculty of the Aleksander Zelwerowicz Theatre Academy, Bialystok branch, with two five-year integrated master's courses in puppet theatre acting and directing, plus a three-year degree in puppet theatre technology opened in 2018. Second, the Puppetry Faculty of the Stanislaw Wyspianski Academy of Theatre Arts, Krakow, at its Wroclaw branch, with puppet theatre acting and puppet theatre directing. Both belong to Polish public arts higher education. Counted by establishment: five courses in total but two schools. Upper bound held at 2, no third course identified. The value does not change but moves from estimated to sourced.
